questions.q: The types of hybrid orbitals of nitrogen in NO$_2^+$, NO$_3^-$, and NH$_4^+$ respectively are
questions.note: The standard answer is (A) sp, sp$^2$, sp$^3$ for NO$_2^+$, NO$_3^-$ and NH$_4^+$ respectively; option (B), which swaps NO$_3^-$ and NH$_4^+$ to sp$^3$ then sp$^2$, does not match their known geometries.
questions.explanation: NO$_2^+$ is linear (sp), NO$_3^-$ is trigonal planar (sp$^2$) and NH$_4^+$ is tetrahedral (sp$^3$), which would give order sp, sp$^2$, sp$^3$ (option A); the KEA key for this version marks option B — the key's answer is retained here (as per KEA key).

questions.q:
In which of the following option/options, the order of arrangement does not agree with the variation of property indicated against it?
(a) BF$_3$ > NF$_3$ > NH$_3$ (Dipole moment)
(b) HgCl$_2$ > NH$_4^+$ > SF$_4$ (Bond angle)
(c) NH$_3$ < H$_2$O < HF (Strength of intermolecular hydrogen bonding)
(d) H - I > H - Br > H - Cl (Bond length)
questions.explanation: Actual dipole moments increase as BF$_3$(0) < NF$_3$ < NH$_3$, so (a) is reversed and disagrees; (b), (c) and (d) correctly represent the bond-angle, H-bond strength and bond-length trends.

questions.q:
With respect to resonance structures of CO$_3^{2-}$ ion, which of the following statements are correct?
(a) All C-O bonds in CO$_3^{2-}$ are equivalent
(b) There are three resonance structures possible for CO$_3^{2-}$ ion
(c) The position of carbon and oxygen should change in every resonance structure
(d) The formal charge on carbon atom is -2
questions.explanation: CO$_3^{2-}$ has three equivalent resonance structures giving equal C-O bond lengths (a, b true); only the double-bond position shifts among the oxygens, carbon's position is fixed (c false); the formal charge on carbon is 0, not -2 (d false).

questions.q: The change in hybridisation (if any) of the 'Al' atom in the following reaction is: AlCl$_3$ + Cl$^-$ $\rightarrow$ AlCl$_4^-$
options: No change in the hybridisation state
questions.explanation: AlCl$_3$ is trigonal planar (sp$^2$); gaining a Cl$^-$ ion makes AlCl$_4^-$ tetrahedral (sp$^3$), so the hybridisation changes from sp$^2$ to sp$^3$.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct option: List-I (Molecule/ion): (a) NO (b) CO (c) O$_2^-$ (d) O$_2$; List-II (Bond order): (i) 1.5 (ii) 2.0 (iii) 2.5 (iv) 3.0
options: a - iv, b - iii, c - ii, d - i
a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
a - i, b - iv, c - iii, d - ii
a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i
questions.explanation: By molecular orbital theory, NO has bond order 2.5, CO has bond order 3.0, O$_2^-$ (superoxide) has bond order 1.5, and O$_2$ has bond order 2.0: a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

questions.q: The electronic configuration of X and Y are given below: X: 1s$^2$ 2s$^2$ 2p$^6$ 3s$^2$ 3p$^3$; Y: 1s$^2$ 2s$^2$ 2p$^6$ 3s$^2$ 3p$^5$. Which of the following is the correct molecular formula and type of bond formed between X and Y?
questions.explanation: X (3p$^3$) is phosphorus (valency 3) and Y (3p$^5$) is chlorine (valency 1); both are non-metals, so they form the covalent compound XY$_3$ (PCl$_3$).

questions.q: A pair of isoelectronic species having bond order of one is
questions.explanation: O$_2^{2-}$ and F$_2$ each have 18 electrons and, by molecular orbital theory, both have a bond order of 1.

questions.q: Which of the following statement is INCORRECT ?
options: Bond length of O$_2$ > Bond length of O$_2^+$
Bond order of O$_2^+$ < Bond order of O$_2^{2-}$
Bond length of O$_2$ < Bond length of O$_2^{2-}$
Bond order of O$_2$ > Bond order of O$_2^{2-}$
questions.explanation: Bond orders are O$_2^+$ = 2.5, O$_2$ = 2 and O$_2^{2-}$ = 1; since 2.5 is greater than 1, the statement that bond order of O$_2^+$ is less than that of O$_2^{2-}$ is false, while the other statements correctly follow from these bond orders.

questions.q: In oxygen and carbon molecule the bonding is
questions.explanation: By molecular orbital theory, O$_2$ (bond order 2) has one net $\sigma$ bond and one net $\pi$ bond (with two unpaired $\pi^*$ electrons); C$_2$ (bond order 2) has two $\pi$ bonds and no $\sigma$ bond, since the $\sigma$2p orbital stays empty.

questions.q: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?
options: Hydrogen bonding is stronger than dispersion forces
Sigma bonds are stronger than π-bonds
σ-electrons are referred to as mobile electrons
questions.explanation: It is the delocalised π-electrons (e.g. in aromatic/conjugated systems), not σ-electrons, that are referred to as mobile electrons; hence statement (D) is incorrect.

questions.q: Bond enthalpies of A$_2$, B$_2$ and AB are in the ratio 2 : 1 : 2. If bond enthalpy of formation of AB is −100 KJ mol$^{-1}$. The bond enthalpy of B$_2$ is
The percentage of s-character in the hybrid orbitals of nitrogen in NO$_2^+$, NO$_3^-$ and NH$_4^+$ respectively are:
questions.explanation: NO$_2^+$ is linear (sp, 50% s), NO$_3^-$ is trigonal planar (sp$^2$, 33.3% s) and NH$_4^+$ is tetrahedral (sp$^3$, 25% s).

questions.q: The formal charge on the central oxygen atom in ozone is
questions.explanation: In the resonance structure of O$_3$, the central O has 3 bonds (one double, one single, counted as 3 sigma+pi bonding pairs shared) and one lone pair: formal charge = 6 - 2 - 3 = +1.

questions.q: Which of the following pair contains 2 lone pairs of electrons on the central atom?
questions.explanation: In I3+ the central I atom has 2 lone pairs (bent shape) and in H2O the central O atom also has 2 lone pairs, so option A is correct.

questions.q: Which of the following possess net dipole moment?
questions.explanation: SO2 has a bent (V-shaped) geometry so its bond dipoles do not cancel, giving it a net dipole moment; BeCl2, BF3 and CO2 are symmetric and non-polar.

questions.q: The number of $\pi$-bonds and $\sigma$-bonds present in naphthalene are respectively
questions.explanation: Naphthalene (C10H8) has 5 C=C double bonds (5 pi bonds) and 19 sigma bonds (11 C-C + 8 C-H).

questions.q: The state of hybrid orbitals of carbon in CO$_2$, CH$_4$ and CO$_3^{2-}$ respectively is
questions.explanation: CO$_2$ is linear (sp), CH$_4$ is tetrahedral (sp$^3$), and CO$_3^{2-}$ is trigonal planar (sp$^2$).

questions.q: Which of the following structure of a molecule is expected to have three bond pairs and one lone pair of electrons ?
questions.explanation: An sp$^3$-hybridised central atom with 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair (as in NH$_3$) adopts a pyramidal shape.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct electron dot structure of N$_2$O molecule ?
options: N=N=O, with two lone pairs on the terminal N and two lone pairs on O, no formal charges
N≡N⁺–O⁻, triple bond between the two N atoms, positive charge on the central N and negative charge with three lone pairs on O
N=N=O, with only one lone pair shown on the terminal N (incomplete octet) and two lone pairs on O
N–N=O, single bond between the two N atoms with one lone pair on the terminal N, double bond to O with two lone pairs
questions.explanation: N$_2$O is best represented by resonance structures with formal charges; as per the KEA key both option B ($:N\equiv N^+-O^-:$) and option C are accepted. Chemically, the two standard resonance contributors are usually A and B, so this question is somewhat ambiguous (as per KEA key).

questions.q: The increasing order of bond order of O$_2$, O$_2^+$, O$_2^-$ and O$_2^{--}$ is
HCl gas is covalent and NaCl is an ionic compound. This is because
options: Electronegativity difference between H and Cl is less than 2.1.
questions.explanation: A small electronegativity difference (H-Cl, < 2.1) favours covalent bonding, while the large Na-Cl difference favours ionic bonding.

questions.q: Main axis of diatomic molecule is Z. The orbitals P$_x$ and P$_y$ overlap to form
questions.explanation: P$_x$ and P$_y$ are perpendicular to the Z internuclear axis and to each other; side-on overlap of parallel p-orbitals (e.g. P$_x$-P$_x$) gives a $\pi$ bond, though since P$_x$ and P$_y$ are mutually perpendicular their net overlap is actually zero (the KEA key accepted both options 1 and 4).

questions.q: The hybridisation of C in diamond, graphite and ethyne is in the order
questions.explanation: Carbon is sp$^3$ hybridised in diamond, sp$^2$ in graphite, and sp in ethyne (triple bond).

questions.q: Using MOT, compare O$_2^+$ and O$_2^-$ species and choose the incorrect option.
options: O$_2^+$ have higher bond order than O$_2^-$.
O$_2^+$ is diamagnetic while O$_2^-$ is paramagnetic.
Both O$_2^+$ and O$_2^-$ are paramagnetic.
questions.explanation: By molecular orbital theory O$_2^+$ (bond order 2.5) has one unpaired electron in $\pi^*$ and O$_2^-$ (bond order 1.5) also has one unpaired electron, so both are paramagnetic; the statement that O$_2^+$ is diamagnetic is incorrect.

questions.q: One of the following conversion results in the change of hybridization and geometry:
questions.explanation: BF$_3$ is sp$^2$ hybridised and trigonal planar, while BF$_4^-$ is sp$^3$ hybridised and tetrahedral, so this conversion changes both the hybridisation and the geometry (unlike NH$_3$$\to$NH$_4^+$ or H$_2$O$\to$H$_3$O$^+$, which stay sp$^3$).

questions.q: The pair of compounds having identical shapes for their molecules is
questions.explanation: XeF$_2$ (sp$^3$d, 3 lone pairs) and ZnCl$_2$ (sp) are both linear molecules despite different hybridisation, while SO$_2$/CO$_2$, BeCl$_2$/ClF$_3$ and CH$_4$/SF$_4$ have different shapes. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: The correct arrangement of the species in the decreasing order of the bond length between carbon and oxygen in them is
questions.explanation: Bond order determines C–O bond length inversely: CO$_3^{2-}$ has the lowest C-O bond order (1.33, most delocalised, longest bond), followed by HCO$_2^-$ (bond order 1.5), then CO$_2$ (bond order 2), and CO has the shortest bond (bond order 3) — giving the decreasing bond length order CO$_3^{2-}$ > HCO$_2^-$ > CO$_2$ > CO.

questions.q: Hybridised states of carbon in Graphite and Diamond are respectively
questions.explanation: Graphite carbon is sp$^2$ hybridised (planar sheets) while diamond carbon is sp$^3$ hybridised (tetrahedral network).

questions.q: Which of the following is diamagnetic ?
questions.explanation: By molecular orbital theory, N$_2$ has all electrons paired (bond order 3, no unpaired electrons), making it diamagnetic, unlike H$_2^+$, He$_2^+$ and O$_2$.

questions.q: The number of antibonding electrons present in O$_2^-$ molecular ion is
questions.explanation: In the valence MO configuration of the superoxide ion O$_2^-$ (17 valence electrons), the antibonding electrons are $\sigma^*2s^2$ and $\pi^*2p^3$, i.e., 5; ambiguity over whether to count 1s core antibonding electrons led KEA to award a grace mark.

questions.q: Which one of the following has NO unpaired electrons?
questions.explanation: By molecular orbital theory, the peroxide ion O$_2^{2-}$ has both antibonding $\pi^*$ orbitals completely filled, giving no unpaired electrons.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a covalent compound?
options: Small difference in electronegativity between the combining atoms.
questions.explanation: Covalent compounds have definite molecular geometry due to directional bonding, so 'no definite geometry' is not a characteristic of covalent compounds.

questions.q: The C-H bond and C-C bond in ethane are formed by which of the following types of overlap?
questions.explanation: Each carbon in ethane is sp$^3$ hybridised; C-H bonds form by sp$^3$-s overlap and the C-C bond forms by sp$^3$-sp$^3$ overlap.

questions.q: Which one of the following contains ionic, covalent and co-ordinate bonds?
questions.note: In CN- the carbon atom carries the terminal lone pair and formal negative charge (:C≡N:-), so Na+ bonds ionically to carbon, giving the standard compound NaCN (option C) with an ionic Na-C bond, a covalent C-N bond, and one coordinate bond within the triple bond (N donating a lone pair to C); KEA's key instead credits NaNC (option D).
questions.explanation: Na-N/C bond is ionic, the C≡N triple bond is covalent, and one of the bonds in the triple bond arises from a coordinate (dative) lone pair donation; KEA's key credits this combination to NaNC (as per KEA key).

questions.q: The percentage of p-character of the hybrid orbitals in graphite and diamond are respectively:
questions.explanation: Graphite carbon is sp$^2$ hybridised (p-character = 2/3 = 67%); diamond carbon is sp$^3$ hybridised (p-character = 3/4 = 75%).

questions.q: When $O_2$ is converted into $O_2^+$; ..............
options: both paramagnetic character and bond order increase
paramagnetic character decreases and the bond order increases
questions.explanation: $O_2$ (bond order 2, 2 unpaired electrons) loses an electron to form $O_2^+$ (bond order 2.5, 1 unpaired electron), so paramagnetism decreases while bond order increases.

questions.q: Increasing order of carbon-carbon bond length for the following is ...........  C$_2$H$_4$ (A), C$_2$H$_2$ (B), C$_6$H$_6$ (C), C$_2$H$_6$ (D)
questions.explanation: Bond length increases as bond order decreases: triple bond (C$_2$H$_2$) < double bond (C$_2$H$_4$) < aromatic bond (C$_6$H$_6$) < single bond (C$_2$H$_6$), giving B < A < C < D.

questions.q: Which one of the following conversions involve change in both hybridization and shape?
questions.explanation: BF$_3$ is sp$^2$ hybridized and trigonal planar, while BF$_4^-$ is sp$^3$ hybridized and tetrahedral, changing both hybridization and shape.

questions.q:
Peroxide ion .......................
a) is diamagnetic.
b) has five completely filled antibonding molecular orbitals.
c) is isoelectronic with neon.
d) has bond order one.
Which one of these is correct?
questions.explanation: O$_2^{2-}$ has all electrons paired (diamagnetic) and bond order 1 (8 bonding, 6 antibonding valence electrons); it is isoelectronic with F$_2$ (not Ne) and has only 3 filled antibonding MOs, so only (a) and (d) are correct.

questions.q: Among the following, the compound that contains ionic, covalent and coordinate linkage is
questions.explanation: NH$_4$Cl has covalent N-H bonds, a coordinate bond forming NH$_4^+$ from NH$_3$ and H$^+$, and an ionic bond between NH$_4^+$ and Cl$^-$.

questions.q: A covalent molecule AB$_3$ has pyramidal structure. The number of lone pair and bond pair electrons in the molecule are respectively
questions.explanation: A pyramidal AB$_3$ molecule (like NH$_3$) has 1 lone pair and 3 bond pairs on the central atom.

questions.q: The correct statement with regard to H$_2^+$ and H$_2^-$ is
options: H$_2^-$ is more stable than H$_2^+$
H$_2^+$ is more stable than H$_2^-$
Both H$_2^+$ and H$_2^-$ are equally stable
Both H$_2^+$ and H$_2^-$ do not exist
questions.explanation: Both have bond order 0.5, but H$_2^-$ has an electron in the antibonding orbital causing extra repulsion, making H$_2^+$ more stable.

questions.q: Arrange the following in the increasing order of their bond order : O$_2$, O$_2^+$, O$_2^-$ and O$_2^{--}$
